purpose: Retained search and material-access record for ecological membership review; taxonomy authority responses are stored separately. Paraphrases below identify the material actually read. None supplies local catch-allocation measurements.

searches.material_read: Repository bibliographic record and complete displayed abstract; primary study PDF not independently read.
searches.paraphrase: Western Bay of Bengal landed-fish study of 1,036 specimens describes bottom omnivory with substantial teleost feeding. Sampled lengths span 21.5–64.4 cm across sexes.
searches.applicability: Species-level evidence supports the Medium benthic-guild extension for Aluterus. Different coast, period and fishery; whole-family Monacanthidae remains heterogeneous and Low. No numerical diet proportion transferred.

searches.material_read: Full online primary article; methods and diet results.
searches.paraphrase: Arabian Gulf stomach sequencing supports coral and sponge feeding in P. maculosus.
searches.applicability: Used to establish a specialised reef-diet mismatch, supporting Very low closest-analogue assignment. DNA-read proportions are not caught mass or trophic diet mass and were not used for weights. Species/site evidence does not establish every angelfish species' diet.

searches.material_read: Search-returned complete ecology account and biological section; direct opening of .org summary returned 403.
searches.version: FishBase account citing Woodland (1990); accessed 30 September 2026
searches.paraphrase: Shallow coastal herbivorous grazing on algae and seagrasses, with incidental invertebrates.
searches.applicability: Supports an explicit mismatch with the source's sole/squilla Benthic Omnivores. Very low approximation retained; neither TL similarity nor genus relationship establishes equivalent guild membership.

searches.material_read: Complete search-returned species account including biology and main reference.
searches.version: FishBase account citing FAO Nakamura (1985); accessed 30 September 2026
searches.paraphrase: Oceanic epipelagic migratory predator, reported depth 0–200 m, feeding on fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods.
searches.applicability: Medium ecological extension to Large Pelagics. Source lists seerfish/barracuda, not sailfish. Offshore and migratory transfer remains assumed; taxonomy remains based on WoRMS.

searches.material_read: Full displayed species account, biology and main reference.
searches.version: FishBase account citing FAO Nakamura (1985); accessed 30 September 2026
searches.paraphrase: Mobile pelagic-oceanic fish and squid predator with substantially broader depth use than the Karnataka model.
searches.applicability: Medium ecological extension, not explicit source membership. No regional composition inferred from global distribution.

searches.query: Ablennes hians FishBase biology and Arabian Sea diet
searches.material_read: Full FishBase biology account; primary journal search-returned title and abstract opening. Direct journal opening timed out; its numerical diet results are not claimed as read.
searches.version: FishBase cites FAO Collette (1999); Roul et al. (2023) journal record, accessed 30 September 2026
searches.paraphrase: Surface neritic/oceanic piscivory is described in the FAO/FishBase account. The independent Kerala diet study sampled 396 specimens in 2015–2017.
searches.applicability: Medium Large Pelagics extension is supported by the accessible biology account. Frozen catch label preserved; the regional study is corroborating bibliographic evidence, not an imported numerical diet or weight.

searches.material_read: Full family account, including feeding remarks; original .org link failed, Stockholm mirror succeeded.
searches.paraphrase: Benthic invertebrate feeding, planktivory and cleaning occur within the family; the modern broad account includes parrotfishes.
searches.applicability: Broad catch-family composition is unknown and historically may differ from modern family treatment. Very low candidate-pool approximation retained. Taxonomic authority is WoRMS; FishBase family listing is not used as nomenclature authority.

searches.query: FAO high seas resources Beryx splendens section 5.3
searches.material_read: Full online section 5.3 of FAO resource assessment.
searches.version: FAO Review of the state of world marine fishery resources, accessed 30 September 2026
searches.paraphrase: Alfonsino occurs from outer shelf around 180 m through continental slope to roughly 1,300 m and around seamounts.
searches.applicability: Depth mismatch supports Very low Large Benthopelagics analogue for Beryx/coarse Berycidae. Global account does not establish Arabian Sea taxon composition.

searches.material_read: Full species account including environment, biology and distribution caveat.
searches.paraphrase: Benthopelagic continental-slope predator at 200–1,100 m; fish, squid and crustacean feeding and upward night migration are described.
searches.applicability: Only a Very low guild analogue. The account's uncertain northern Indian Ocean occurrence statement does not authorize relabelling the observed catch.

searches.material_read: Complete search-returned NOAA account including biological and research sections.
searches.version: NOAA Fisheries Opah Science, accessed 30 September 2026
searches.paraphrase: Deep open-ocean habitat and squid/deep-water-fish foraging are described. NOAA notes multiple opah species and Pacific biological-data limitations.
searches.applicability: Very low closest ecological analogue. Pacific observations do not establish Arabian Sea species identity or caught composition. The appendix cites this accessible authority without unsupported numerical depth claims.

searches.material_read: No reliably retrieved biological passage; direct retrieval repeatedly timed out.
searches.applicability: Not relied on for an independently verified numerical depth range. Accessible NOAA material supports the retained weak analogue; the concise Sources entry was corrected accordingly.
